content.intro: Handling Missing Data is part of Data Cleaning and Manipulation. Start with identifying missing values and connect it to the worked example and expected result.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Missingness can be accidental or meaningful; deletion or imputation changes the analysis. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Count missing cells first, state a handling rule, and compare row counts before and after. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Handling Missing Data
content_blocks.code: aggregate(amount ~ region, data = data.frame(region = c("W", "E", "W"), amount = c(8, 5, 7)), sum)
content_blocks.expected_output: Group E sums to 5; group W sums to 15.

content_blocks.limitations: Grouped summaries reduce rows but should preserve meaningful group keys. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For handling missing data, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Removing rows before measuring how much information is missing.
common_mistakes.why: Missingness or outliers may be systematic and can bias the result.
common_mistakes.fix: Count affected rows, state the rule, compare before/after summaries and keep an audit trail.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating every repeated key as an accidental duplicate.
common_mistakes.why: Repeated rows may represent repeated events or valid measurements.
common_mistakes.fix: Define the expected key grain and review examples before deleting records.

common_mistakes.problem: Changing categories or units without documenting the transformation.
common_mistakes.why: Silent standardization makes results difficult to reproduce.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the mapping rule and add a validation check.
